A Lagos-based lawyer, Emmanuel Umohinyang, has urged the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, to strengthen security measures and prevent political violence ahead of the forthcoming general election. Umohinyang, in a letter dated November 16, 2026, addressed to the IG at the Force Headquarters, Abuja, and obtained by The PUNCH on Wednesday, expressed concern over reported attacks on political campaign convoys, rallies, supporters and other legitimate political activities across the country. He warned that the growing tendency for political disagreements to degenerate into physical attacks, intimidation and destruction of property posed a serious threat to Nigeria’s democratic process. The lawyer urged the police not to wait until violence erupted before responding, but to identify potential flashpoints, assess security threats and take preventive measures. He described the forthcoming election as an opportunity for Disu to demonstrate purposeful leadership and the capacity of the police to protect Nigerians irrespective of their political affiliations. He said, “The security of lives and property and the protection of citizens’ constitutional rights must not be compromised by the desperation and intolerance that appears to accompany the struggle for political power. “The responsibility of the police, therefore, is not merely to restore order after violence has occurred but, more importantly, to anticipate threats, identify potential flashpoints and prevent foreseeable violence.” The lawyer called for professional reorientation, institutional sanitisation and operational mobilisation of police personnel across the country. Return of violent campaigns ‘Politicians must emulate Jonathan’s 2015 election concession’ Police arrest four suspected armed robbers in Cross River He also cautioned the police against allowing themselves to be used as instruments of political intimidation or manipulated into compromising citizens’ rights. Umohinyang stressed the need for equal protection for supporters of the ruling and opposition parties, insisting that police protection should not be determined by political affiliation, ethnicity, religion or other considerations. He urged the IGP to issue clear directives to commissioners of police in the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory to strengthen security arrangements and adopt intelligence-driven policing. He said, “They must not adopt a complacent or reactive posture while political tensions build up around them. Rather, they must be proactive and intelligence-driven. They must identify emerging threats, monitor potential flashpoints, assess credible security information and take timely preventive measures.” The lawyer further called for prompt investigation of attacks on political activities and the prosecution of perpetrators, sponsors and accomplices where credible evidence established their involvement. He also urged the police chief to ensure that officers found guilty of negligence, dereliction of duty or complicity in political violence faced appropriate disciplinary and legal consequences. Umohinyang said the President’s position against political violence should be reflected in police operations, stressing that those responsible for sponsoring or perpetrating attacks should not escape justice because of their political influence. He said, “The forthcoming election should be an opportunity for Nigerians to exercise their democratic rights peacefully, not a period of apprehension in which citizens fear attending rallies, joining campaign processions or expressing their political preferences. “The safety of Nigerians must never be negotiable, and no political ambition is worth the loss of a single innocent life.” Dayo Oyewo Dayo is a journalist at Punch Newspapers with over nine years of experience covering politics, entertainment, crime, and environmental conservation.
